raw/eyeline/run.stdout.txt:39-41 'FINDING Traefik on port 80 has authentication OFF (reachable from the internet) ... --api.insecure=true exposes the Traefik dashboard/API with no auth. It is reachable from the internet.' Also stdout:78, report.json:2124 and :2399, ranked #1 in report.html:128 'Start here'. On port 80 the dashboard/API is served only through the D3 router, and that router returns 401 without credentials (pre-run O3: 401). api.insecure serves the API on 8080 only. The claim is false, and it is the alarm D3 was built to draw ('Traefik dashboard exposed without auth' on port 80). Mechanism: riders.auth repeats the container's auth state for every port the container publishes (report.json:2395-2414). Disputable: a lenient grader could call this a mis-attributed duplicate of K3 rather than a judgment on the D3 route, which would give 0 false alarms; K3 reach would then be stated both as internet (stdout:39-40, 78) and LAN (stdout:43-44, 79), a contradiction the key counts as overstated, so reach accuracy becomes 5 correct / 1 overstated / 1 understated.

The engine was frozen at 21:01:59Z, before up.sh started (21:08:32Z), and verified 23/23 before the run, so this could not shape the engine. Whether the building session read the lab/ files' contents when copying them is not recorded (grader's statement).

E-b (blindness): the grader's stage-1 report to the building session said the total scores out of 9, that K9 concerns sshd passwordauthentication, that the UFW baseline holds, that one item's reach is host-local, that 10 containers were up, and that a loopback-only DNAT rule was confirmed. All of this came after the engine freeze (21:01:59Z), and no engine change followed (23/23 verified before the run by the coordinator, and again by the grader at grading time).

E-c (record): the coordinator's stage-2 message called the run a '26-port plan, same as 17.5'. The run's own plan is 28 ports (run.stdout.txt:13; report.json:1460): 25 fixed ports plus the inside listeners 8081, 11434 and 61208 (eyeline_engine/probe.py:18-31). The settings were the same; the count follows the lab.

E-d (method): the pre-run O8 and after-run A3 port loops print 'closed' for both refused and timed-out connects (timeout 5 s, not the key's 4 s), so they do not separate closed from filtered. eyeline saw 5432 as 'filtered' (run.stdout.txt:22). Both agree that nothing is reachable from the internet.

E-e (method): A4 kept the values in a Python process's memory instead of the key's umask-077 /tmp file, and searched each value's first 16 characters plus case, HTML-entity, JSON and whitespace variants. That is stricter than the key, and the result is the same: 0.
